"No app," said Avni, tapping the canteen table. "A group chat, a bag of clothes, and us."
"Us carrying bags? In front of everyone?" Ankita winced.
"Block C only, this Monday. We collect at seven, drop at the laundry, deliver on Thursday. Fifteen rupees a bag."
"And if nobody signs up?"
"Then we learn that before spending months on code."
"Fine. Poster?"
"Just a note on each door."
On Monday night the chat had nine names. On the next Thursday they carried the last bag up three floors. Ankita dropped it at a door and grinned. "Fourteen bags the first week. People actually paid." Avni was counting coins into a tin, barely listening. "Week two, then. We see if they come back."

qa.a: Ankita feels embarrassed and unsure, wincing at the thought of carrying bags in front of everyone.

qa.a: They could ask the paying customers what they liked and what nearly stopped them, because a small paying group can explain what a poster cannot.

qa.a: A student in Block C gets a note on the door, gives a bag at seven and gets it back on Thursday, so it looks like a simple, cheap favour with a clear price.

passage: In our third year, Arnab and I were sure the hostel needed a laundry app. I'm Lalit. We'd even sketched the screens. Then a senior asked us, "Has anyone paid you yet?" Nobody had. So instead of coding for three months, we made a chat group for one hostel block, Block C, and posted: "Laundry pickup Tuesday and Friday, 12 rupees a piece, washed and folded by the next evening." We collected the bags ourselves from the corridor, carried them to the laundromat near the gate on a borrowed cycle, and wrote every order in a notebook. For two weeks we did it all by hand. Twenty-three people ordered. Nine ordered twice. My shoulders ached from the bags. Looking back, those two weeks taught us more than any app would have: people would pay, but mostly just before exams.

qa.q: How many people ordered in two weeks?
How did Lalit feel during the two weeks?
qa.a: Lalit felt tired, with aching shoulders, but encouraged as real orders came in.

qa.q: What else could the pair try after the two weeks?
qa.a: They could run the same manual service in a second block or in exam weeks to see if demand holds, before building any app.

qa.q: How might the Block C residents see the service?
qa.a: Residents get cheap, easy laundry, and by ordering they show the founders whether people will really pay.

grounding: Shows founders running a manual laundry pickup for one hostel block through a chat group for two weeks, instead of coding an app, to see if anyone pays.

Hostel warden's note, Block A, end of February.
For the past two weeks, Tanuja and Ishita from third year have run a laundry pickup service for this block by hand. They asked my permission first and posted the details on the block's chat group: pickup on Monday and Thursday evenings, 15 rupees a piece, returned in two days. No app, just a notebook and a list on the notice board.
I watched them drag bags down the stairs twice a week and fold clothes in the common room. Some residents were doubtful at first. By the second week the list had thirty-one names, and several students asked if it would continue during exams.
Tanuja told me they want to build an app, but wanted proof first that people would pay. I thought that was sensible.
Next step: they have asked to use the common room on Thursday evenings next month. I've agreed.

qa.q: How much did the service charge per piece?
Why did Tanuja want to run it by hand first?
qa.a: Tanuja felt cautious about building an app too soon and wanted proof that people would pay before investing in one.

qa.q: What else could the pair track during the next month?
qa.a: They could note how many people order again and in which weeks, so they know whether demand lasts beyond the first try.

qa.q: How does the warden see the project?
qa.a: The warden finds the approach sensible, notes the growing list of names, and supports it by allowing use of the common room.

grounding: Illustrates founders testing a laundry idea as a hand-run pickup service for one block for two weeks before building any app.
